name: Back Alley
description: Back Alley is a robust partnership trick-taking game that originated in the American military. It combines the bidding intensity of Spades with the fluctuating hand sizes of Oh Hell!. Played with two unique Jokers known as 'Bloopers', the game follows a 26-hand schedule that tests a team's ability to communicate and predict trick counts under constantly changing conditions. Its reputation is built on high-pressure bidding where missing a contract results in severe point penalties.

history.origins: Back Alley, also called Back Alley Bridge or Back Street Bridge, originated in the American military, probably during World War II. It grew out of servicemen’s barracks games and spread through off-base social circles as a high-intensity partnership trick-taking game.
timeline: 1940s: Early versions played in the US Army and Navy.
1960s: Deployment of 'Bloopers' (Jokers) becomes standard during the Vietnam War era.
1980s: Standardized rules appear in military recreation handbooks.
Present: Popular in veteran communities and regional US trick-taking circles.
history.cultural: Known for vocal 'trash talking' and intense partnership coordination, reflecting its military social upbringing.
history.evolution: The game was originally played without Jokers (using 2s as high trumps), but the modern 'Blooper' version is now the definitive standard.

setup.players: 4 players in North-South and East-West partnerships.
setup.deck: 54 cards including Big Joker and Little Joker.
setup.dealing: Deal starts at 13 cards each. Subsequent hands decrease by 1 until the 1-card hand, then increase back to 13, for a full 26-deal 13‑1‑13 schedule.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, 2 distinct Jokers, score sheet.

rules.objective: Accumulate the highest score by accurately bidding and winning tricks over the full hand schedule.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Lead**: Left of dealer leads any card. 2. **Following Suit**: Players must follow suit if possible. 3. **The Bloopers**: The Big Blooper is the highest trump, followed by the Little Blooper. If led to a trick, the leader names the suit it represents. 4. **Winning Tricks**: Highest trump or highest card of lead suit wins.
keyRules: Board (Bid of 13): A team that bids all tricks accurately in a 13-card hand wins a massive bonus (or the whole game).
Overtricks: Teams are credited for tricks won beyond their bid, but at a lower point value.
Undertricks: A team that fails to reach their combined bid is 'set' and loses significant points.

strategy.basic: In the large-hand deals (13-10), bid conservatively. The penalty for overbidding is much harsher than the reward for overtricks.
strategy.intermediate: Use 'Blooper' leads. If you have the Big Blooper, lead it early to smoke out the opponents' trump Aces or the Little Blooper.
strategy.advanced: The 'One-Card Hand' (Suicide): When you only have one card, the bidding is pure luck unless you hold a Joker or the Ace of Trumps. Use it as a moment to calibrate your team's overall risk profile.
tips: If your partner bids high (e.g., 5 or 6), only bid your absolute sure tricks. Don't 'double down' and risk putting your team into an unmakeable contract.
Remember: It is 100% legal to win more tricks than you bid. 'Bags' (the overtrick penalty in Spades) do not exist hereâ€”overtricks are pure profit.

variations.name: Army Straight
variations.description: Played without Jokers; the 2 of the trump suit is the highest card in the game.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This version removes jokers and promotes the two of trump, but detailed engine overrides are not yet encoded.

variations.name: Back Alley Bridge
variations.description: Bidding is done by teams simultaneously using signals rather than in rotation.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation changes only bidding communication style; the base deal, play, and scoring engines stay as in standard Back Alley.

scoring.description: Scoring is calculated per team after each deal.

synthesis.shortDescription: Strap in for the ultimate partnership challenge. Back Alley takes you through a grueling 25-hand campaign where hand sizes shrink and grow, and two 'Blooper' Jokers reign supreme. Coordinate with your partner, hit your targets, and avoid the devastating negative scores in this military-grade classic.
